provenance.citation: Hu D., Beauvais M. L., Kamm G. E., Mullens B. G., Sanchez Monserrate B. A., Vornholt S. M., Chupas P. J., Chapman K. W., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 145 (2023) 26545-26549, doi 10.1021/jacs.3c10916

provenance.verification_todo: Spot-check 5-10 points per panel against the printed figure (for example Li2TiO3 at 0.5, 1, 2, 5 min and the time anatase reaches zero) and compare reconstruction.png with Fig. 2.

system.reaction: anatase TiO2 + Li2CO3 -> Li2TiO3 (+ CO2) -> Li4Ti5O12; anatase -> rutile in parallel
system.mixing: 5:2 TiO2:Li2CO3 molar ratio, pelletized, loaded in a capillary
system.initiation: sample moved into a pre-heated hot zone, heating in under 10 s (grey 'Heating' strip in Fig. 3, about the first 0.17 min)
system.atmosphere_note: not stated in the main text

files.extracted_phase_fractions.csv: Fig. 2: weight % of each phase and Ti-mole fractions on a 0.05 min grid from 0.05 min to the end of each panel (10 min; 9.76 min at 750 C). Columns wt_* sum to 100 by construction (the figure is a normalised stack). tifrac_* are the fractions of Ti in each Ti-bearing phase, computed from wt_* with nominal molar masses (TiO2 79.866, Li2TiO3 109.75, Li4Ti5O12 459.08 g/mol, 1, 1, 5 Ti per formula unit).
files.fig3_482C_li2tio3_relative.csv: Fig. 3: Li2TiO3 at 482 C in arbitrary units (the y axis has no ticks). Values are the fraction of the image height above the x axis, so only the shape and ratios of slopes are meaningful, not absolute amounts. Time 0 to 5 min on a 0.02 min grid.
files.reconstruction.png: Our own re-plot of the extracted curves for comparison with the printed figures.

checks_done: Initial wt % at 0.05 min: anatase about 75, Li2CO3 about 25; the 5:2 molar mix gives 73 / 27.
Maximum Li2TiO3 is 54.2 / 55.4 / 53.7 wt % (700 / 725 / 750 C) against about 52 wt % stated in the text: a bias of about 2 wt %, most likely from the thick boundary lines (5.7 px per wt %).
Fig. 3 slope ratio, 0.25-0.75 min versus 1-2 min, is 4.1, matching the authors' statement that the fast regime is 4 times the later rate.
caveats: Weight fractions are normalised to the remaining solid, and CO2 leaves as gas, so wt % has no conserved total. Use the Ti-mole fractions (tifrac_*) for balance checks. Li2CO3 carries no Ti and is tracked in wt % only.
Li2TiO3 is reported by the authors to be Li-deficient (Li2-xTiO3-x, peak 52 wt % above the 48 wt % stoichiometric maximum), so the nominal molar mass makes the Ti fraction slightly approximate.
The first 0.2-0.3 min (heating) is unreliable: the axis line and the vertical Li2CO3 label overlap the data, and the t = 0 column is dropped.

A thin cyan Li2CO3 strip of about 1 wt % runs along the top of every panel to 10 min. It is probably a line-width artefact (the text says Li2CO3 peaks are no longer distinguishable after about 30 s). Treat Li2CO3 below about 2 wt % as zero.
Boundary lines are 1-2 px thick, so phase fractions carry roughly 1-2 wt % of systematic error. Anatase reaching exactly zero is read from where the red line meets the axis.
One chemistry, one lab, one capillary geometry. Use as a sanity benchmark, not as evidence about solid-state synthesis in general.
